title: Greedy (exchange argument, scheduling) — Depth Pass
relevance: High — post-ladder CF Div2 C/D scheduling & custom-comparator greeds; these are the forms that show up once Movie-Festival / Tasks-Deadlines templates are automatic.
company_notes: Average-grade / median-salary minimize-cost → deficit fill or BS-on-median + greedy assign (Vanya / Salary Changing). k servers / 2 machines / reusable interval licenses → sort by start/end + multiset of free end times (Two TVs → TV Shows; Meeting-Rooms II). One machine with release times & deadlines → PQ of earliest deadlines among released jobs (Printing Machine). Bulk discount / 2-for-1 once bill passes a threshold → two-pointer or reverse spend unlocked by expensive items (PriceFixed).

phases.goal: Spot post-template greeds that need a custom exchange comparator, BS+greedy feasibility, or an available-job priority queue rather than plain sort-by-end.

must_hit.point: After classic sort-by-end / duration / deadline, deeper greeds ask for a custom comparator from an n=2 exchange, a feasibility check under a guessed answer, or a PQ over currently available jobs (earliest exit / reverse-from-deadline).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names those three shapes: exchange comparator, BS+greedy check, or available-pool earliest-exit / reverse-from-deadline.

must_hit.point: Recognize them when item order changes the objective by a closed-form delta, when you can binary-search a time/cost and simulate, or when idle gaps must be jumped while always serving the tightest live deadline.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites closed-form swap delta, binary-search-and-simulate, or jump-idle + tightest live deadline as the cue.

must_hit.point: OA/interview disguises include deficit fill or BS-on-median hire salary, k servers / 2 machines / reusable licenses with a multiset of free ends, one-machine release+deadline PQ, and 2-for-1 bulk-discount buy order.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to Vanya/Salary Changing, Two TVs/TV Shows/Meeting-Rooms II, Printing Machine, or PriceFixed-style discount unlock.

probes: What tells you this is beyond classic sort-by-end Movie-Festival greedy?
Is the tell a swap-derived comparator, a binary-searched answer with a greedy check, or an available-job priority queue?

hints.1: Ask whether plain earliest-end / deadline sort already finishes the classic ladder.
hints.2: Look for closed-form order delta, guessed time/cost to simulate, or idle jumps with a live deadline pool.
hints.3: Name n=2 exchange comparator, BS+greedy feasibility, or earliest-exit / reverse-from-deadline PQ, and match to Stas, Delivery Dilemma / Schedule Management, or Printing Machine.

phases.goal: Choose the right deep-greedy family and justify the sort key or simulation order with exchange or feasibility structure.

must_hit.point: n=2 exchange → comparator: expand the objective for adjacent i,j; the sign of Δ after a swap is the sort key (Stas: sort by b−a).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Expands adjacent cost, takes the sign of the swap delta as the comparator, and cites Stas / b−a.

must_hit.point: BS + greedy check: guess time/cost/mid; simulate a clear greedy (assign hardest constraints first, dump remainder cheaply)—Delivery Dilemma, Schedule Management, Exams, Salary Changing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says binary-search the answer then run a feasibility greedy that prioritizes hard constraints and dumps the rest cheaply.

must_hit.point: Reverse-from-deadline: when once available, always available, process time backward and always take the best live job (Portals / Money Buys / USACO milk-scheduling pattern).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Processes backward and repeatedly picks the best still-live job under the always-available assumption.

must_hit.point: Available-pool + earliest exit: keep started jobs in a min-heap of deadlines; on idle, jump to the next arrival (Printing Machine)—exchange: always print the live job that leaves first.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maintains a deadline min-heap of released jobs and jumps idle time to the next arrival instead of walking every time unit.

probes: What do you sort by, and how does an adjacent-swap delta justify that comparator?
Would you binary-search an answer and check greedily, or maintain an available-job heap—and why?

hints.1: Decide exchange-comparator vs BS+check vs available-pool before coding.
hints.2: For order-sensitive cost, expand adjacent i,j and sort by sign of Δ; for monotone feasibility, guess mid and simulate.
hints.3: Stas → sort by b−a; Delivery/Schedule/Exams/Salary → BS+greedy; Printing Machine → deadline PQ + idle jump; Portals/Money Buys → reverse best-live.

phases.goal: Show concrete mechanics for the core templates on the depth ladder: gaps, Huffman merges, closed forms, resource multisets, and conflict pairing.

must_hit.point: Tape: cover with k segments by taking total span minus the (k-1) largest inter-break gaps.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Computes full span, drops the (k-1) largest gaps between consecutive points, and sums the rest.

must_hit.point: Stick Divisions / Huffman: repeatedly combine the two current smallest costs; any other merge order can be exchanged toward this without raising cost.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Always merges the two smallest with a heap/PQ and cites the exchange argument for that order.

must_hit.point: Reading Books closed form is max(sum, 2·max); Gap/resource reuse: Two TVs / TV Shows track free end-times in a multiset; Fugitive matches sorted gaps to bridges with multiset lower_bound tightest fit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States max(sum, 2·max) and/or multiset of free ends / lower_bound gap-to-bridge assignment.

must_hit.point: PriceFixed: buy cheapest from the left while unlocking discounts from the right (two pointers); Pairs of Segments: sort by end and when a conflict appears kill the farther-reaching partner.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes left-cheap / right-unlock two pointers, or end-sorted conflict resolution against the farthest intruder.

must_hit.point: Air Conditioner maintains a feasible [lo,hi] grown/shrunk by elapsed time between customers and rejects when empty; Counting Kangaroos nests with sort + two pointers and at most ⌊n/2⌋ pockets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Updates a moving temperature window by elapsed time, or nests smaller into larger with the ⌊n/2⌋ bound.

probes: How do you turn covering points with k tape segments into a gap calculation?
Walk through Stick Divisions’ merge rule and Reading Books’ closed form.

hints.1: Pick one core mechanic: gaps, two-smallest merges, or free-end multiset.
hints.2: Tape = span − (k-1) largest gaps; Stick Divisions always merges two smallest; Reading Books → max(sum, 2·max).
hints.3: Also: Two TVs/TV Shows free-end multiset, Fugitive lower_bound bridges, PriceFixed left/right unlock, Pairs of Segments kill farthest intruder.

phases.goal: Avoid time-range simulation and rely on event-driven heaps/multisets for available jobs and reusable resources.

must_hit.point: Do not simulate every timestamp to 10^18; on idle, jump to the next arrival (Printing Machine available-pool).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses looping over the full time axis to 10^18 and jumps idle time to the next job arrival.

must_hit.point: Available-pool keeps started jobs in a min-heap of deadlines; resource reuse keeps a multiset of free end-times (Two TVs / TV Shows); size-capped priority queues appear in sliding top-k loot (Knights).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names deadline min-heap, free-end multiset, and/or size-capped loot PQ as the working structures.

must_hit.point: Gap matching (Fugitive) sorts gaps and bridges then assigns with multiset lower_bound rather than scanning all pairs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts both sides and uses lower_bound tightest-fit assignment instead of pairwise search.

probes: Why is simulating every time unit dangerous on large time bounds, and what do you do instead?
Which heap or multiset operations replace a full time-axis or all-pairs scan here?

hints.1: Large horizons make per-timestamp loops unsafe.
hints.2: Jump idle to the next arrival; store live deadlines or free ends in a heap/multiset.
hints.3: Cite not simulating to 10^18, Printing Machine idle jump, free-end multiset, and Fugitive lower_bound matching.

phases.goal: Catch invalid comparators, unnecessary simulation, and wrong conflict or merge choices the depth ladder punishes.

must_hit.point: If the exchange-derived comparator is not a total order, the greedy is wrong.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks that the sort key induces a valid total order before trusting the greedy order.

must_hit.point: Don’t over-simulate two pointers for Reading Books when the bottleneck is the single longest book—the answer is max(sum, 2·max).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the closed form and refuses an elaborate pairing simulation once the longest book is the bottleneck.

must_hit.point: On available-pool scheduling, do not simulate every timestamp to 10^18; jump idle to the next arrival.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects a time-loop approach to event jumps on the Printing Machine pattern.

must_hit.point: Conflict pairing: sort by end and resolve the earliest-ending conflict against the farthest intruder—not an arbitrary intersecting partner (Pairs of Segments).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts by end and always kills the farther-reaching partner of the earliest conflict.

probes: When does an adjacent-swap comparator fail even if the delta formula looks right?
What goes wrong if you simulate Reading Books or Printing Machine more heavily than needed?

hints.1: Ask whether the comparator is a total order and whether a closed form already exists.
hints.2: Invalid total order → wrong greedy; Reading Books → max(sum, 2·max); Printing Machine → jump idle, don’t walk to 10^18.
hints.3: Also for intersecting removals: earliest-ending conflict vs farthest-reaching partner, not a random pair.

tradeoffs.topic: Custom n=2 exchange comparator vs classic sort-by-end
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When order changes the objective by a closed-form adjacent delta, expand cost for i,j and sort by the sign of Δ (Stas: b−a). Classic earliest-end / duration keys are not enough once Movie-Festival / Tasks-Deadlines templates are automatic.

tradeoffs.topic: Binary-search + greedy check vs one-pass schedule
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When feasibility is monotone in a guessed time/cost/mid, binary-search the answer and simulate a clear greedy (hardest constraints first, dump remainder cheaply)—Delivery Dilemma, Schedule Management, Exams, Salary Changing—rather than inventing a single forward pass.

tradeoffs.topic: Forward available-pool earliest exit vs reverse-from-deadline
tradeoffs.strong_answer: If jobs have release times and you serve from a live pool, keep a min-heap of deadlines and jump idle to the next arrival (Printing Machine). When once available, always available, process time backward and always take the best live job (Portals / Money Buys).

tradeoffs.topic: Huffman two-smallest merges vs other merge orders
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Stick Divisions repeatedly combines the two current smallest costs; any other merge order can be exchanged toward this without raising cost.

tradeoffs.topic: Closed form vs two-pointer simulation (Reading Books)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: After the greedy pairing insight, the answer is max(sum, 2·max); don’t over-simulate two pointers when the bottleneck is the single longest book.
For 2-for-1 threshold buys, use two pointers: buy cheapest from the left while unlocking discounts from the right (or reverse spend unlocked by expensive items).

gotchas.trap: Using an exchange-derived sort key that is not a total order.
gotchas.correction: The sign of Δ after an adjacent swap is only valid as a comparator if it defines a total order; otherwise the greedy is wrong.

gotchas.trap: Simulating every timestamp out to 10^18 on release/deadline single-machine scheduling.
gotchas.correction: Keep started jobs in a min-heap of deadlines; on idle, jump to the next arrival (Printing Machine).

gotchas.trap: Over-simulating Reading Books with elaborate two-pointer pairing.
gotchas.correction: The answer is max(sum, 2·max) once the single longest book is the bottleneck.

gotchas.trap: Covering points with k tape segments without dropping the right gaps.
gotchas.correction: Total span minus the (k-1) largest inter-break gaps.

gotchas.trap: Merging sticks in an arbitrary order.
gotchas.correction: Always combine the two current smallest costs; other orders exchange toward Huffman without lowering cost.

gotchas.trap: Resolving intersecting segment pairs by removing an arbitrary overlapping partner.
gotchas.correction: Sort by end; when a conflict appears, kill the farther-reaching partner (Pairs of Segments).

gotchas.trap: Treating Petya and Exam like a different cutoff template (e.g. 978G).
gotchas.correction: Sort by time and try every last-mandatory cutoff; it is not the same as 978G.
